title: Decoupled boundary-layer optimization with frozen central cavity
scientific_hypothesis: Layers 4-11 have converged to a local optimum contributing minimally to score improvement; restricting optimization to boundary layers 0-3 and 12-15 while freezing the central 8 layers will reduce search dimensionality and enable finer convergence on the sensitivity-critical entrance and exit interfaces.
design_principle: Freeze converged strata to eliminate wasted optimization budget; apply asymmetric step sizing based on observed oscillation magnitude per layer from iteration 20 results.
proposed_topology: 16-layer alternating stack: ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS|ZnSe|ZnS on Ge substrate, with layers 4-11 thickness fixed at [411, 966, 878, 1273, 500, 465, 454, 403] nm and layers 0-3, 12-15 optimizable
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Fixed central layers reduce deposition complexity variability
theory_basis: Gradient-based optimization efficiency improves when dimensionality is reduced by fixing converged parameters
Boundary layers in dichroic stacks typically dominate impedance matching at air-film and film-substrate interfaces
expected_advantages: Reduced search space enables finer convergence on critical layers
Eliminates oscillation in already-converged central layers
known_risks: Freezing suboptimal central layers may prevent escape from local optimum
Boundary-layer-only optimization may not capture coupling effects with central cavity
execution_request_english: Optimize a fixed 16-layer alternating ZnSe/ZnS multilayer stack on Ge substrate at normal incidence. Initialize with thicknesses [1130, 874, 481, 227, 411, 966, 878, 1273, 500, 465, 454, 403, 275, 938, 733, 1257] nm. Freeze layers 4-11 (indices 4 through 11 inclusive) at their current values. Optimize only layers 0, 1, 2, 3, 12, 13, 14, 15 with bounds ±40 nm from initialization. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Evaluate mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band (maximize) and 3000-5000 nm band (minimize) with equal weighting. Total layer count: 16 finite layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 8000-11000 nm, 3000-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band; Low transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count not exceeding 16.
revision_reason: Responds to feedback directive to decouple parameter update schedule by freezing converged layers 4-11 and restricting optimization to 8 boundary layers. Addresses score stagnation observed in rounds 3-5.
